model.name: Codex (GPT-5 family)
model.note: The requested GPT-5.6 Sol product label was not exposed by this session.

scope.purpose: Determine whether approximately 29 far stars can become visually stationary relative to the fighter playfield and cease participating in the per-world-step erase/resolve/render path.

git.runtimeBaseline: PASS_FIT combined PMG pickup plus unhooked contiguous 187-byte primitive

method.classification: instruction-exact measurement of the current linked far-star routines plus static analysis of the rotating LMS ring
inputs: current linked runtime and symbol file
method.measurement: A bounded NMOS-6502 instruction trace initialized all 29 records as visible, measured the complete erase path, forced the non-far-step post-rotation resolve/render path, and triggered one eligible twinkle slot. Visible accesses were counted only when the effective address was inside the gameplay screen/ring.

currentFarStarPath.visualCadence: Every authoritative world-row event erases all visible far-star overlays, rotates the physical row mapping, then resolves/renders all records. Logical far-star rows advance only on the 1/4-rate far step, but the visual relocation remains required on the other 3/4 steps.

twinkle.reportedBoundCycles: 166-168 depending on the selected row/address path
twinkle.reason: The world-step erase makes records non-visible before tick_star_twinkle, so the visible twinkle write does not coexist with the 4221-cycle peak.

currentFarStarPath.bookkeepingExcludedFrom4221: Logical 1/4-rate row advance, respawn RNG and cadence selection are simulation, not visible commit work. Setting far_star_speed to zero would remove some simulation but not the 4221-cycle visual relocation.

ringInvariant.operation: The old logical-bottom physical row is filled from the divider, PLAYFIELD_ROW_LO/HI entries shift toward larger logical row numbers, and the recycled physical row becomes logical row zero for the next display list.
ringInvariant.consequence: A byte left in a rotating physical row appears one logical screen row lower after publication. Therefore a sparse pattern baked into physical/base rows moves with the world ring; it is not screen-stationary.
ringInvariant.formalCondition: For an unchanged physical sparse pattern P to remain identical at screen coordinates across a one-row ring rotation, every unchanged row would need P[row+1] = P[row]. An arbitrary 29-point distribution does not satisfy this; only vertically repeated patterns such as stripes do, and those are not visually equivalent to 29 stars.
ringInvariant.screenStationaryRequirement: Keeping 29 arbitrary points fixed at fighter-screen coordinates requires changing their physical destination after each ring rotation, which is the current erase/resolve/render class of work.

variants.name: static physical-screen stars
variants.reason: If bytes are left in physical ring rows they visibly move with the DLIST rotation. If their screen coordinates are held fixed, all 29 must still be relocated after every world-row event; zero logical speed does not remove the current visual path.

variants.name: stars baked into recycled/base row
variants.representation: A deterministic 28-row pattern with one far star per row and a second star in one row preserves 29 visible points after warm-up; column/code entries preserve brightness and size variety.
variants.readsPerRecycle: 1-3 bounded occupancy tests with a fallback column
variants.reasonRejected: The stars become part of world/base rows and move at the full ring cadence. Near stars would no longer be the sole moving/parallax star layer, contrary to the owner-approved screen-static direction.

variants.name: sparse deterministic background pattern
variants.worldRowKeyedMode: Equivalent to Variant B: inexpensive generation on recycle, but the points move with the ring.
variants.screenRowKeyedMode: Preserves screen coordinates only by regenerating/relocating the sparse pattern after each ring rotation, restoring the per-world-step writer cost.
variants.reason: Changing table lookup into procedural generation does not change the row-mapping invariant.

chosenRepresentation.reason: No evaluated representation simultaneously removes the dynamic 29-star path and preserves visually stationary far stars under the current ring architecture.
chosenRepresentation.prototypeDecision: No runtime prototype was justified: Variant A/C fail structurally, while Variant B's only unresolved property is an owner-visible motion change, not CPU feasibility.

visualResult.counterfactualVariantB: Retains 29 points and glyph variety but scrolls them with the base ring at full world speed.

counterfactualRowBakedDesign.gate: PASS numerically, but not an acceptable screen-static implementation

verySlowSparseTwinkle.constraint: No 29-record erase/render pass. The event would need to be kept out of the narrow legal Spread window if Variant B were ever authorized.

writerSites.note: Variant B removes six independent far-star/twinkle sites. Its one bounded base-row generation access belongs to base construction before projectile publication and is not a later independent far-star writer.

counterfactualRowBakedDesign.classification: STRONG_PASS numerically; invalid for the required motion contract

counterfactualRowBakedDesign.spreadClassification: Fits arithmetically without twinkle but remains high-risk and below the prior strong-pass margin.

capacityForecast.classification: ESTIMATE; visual-window cost only, before Light weapons and without implementing Light

ownerCompliantStaticDesign.result: Neither path fits because no far-star cycles are recovered.

counterfactualRowBakedDesign.result: Window path is numerically preserved before Light weapons, but this result is conditional on accepting full-speed far-star motion.

ownerCompliantStaticDesign.reason: The current relocation mechanism remains required.

counterfactualRowBakedDesign.classification: ESTIMATE only; no source or placement change was made

stopCondition.reason: The rotating LMS ring forces all 29 screen-stationary far stars to be relocated on every world-row event. Baking only at row recycle removes the cost solely by changing them into full-speed moving background points.

verification.build: not rerun because no runtime/generated file changed; current XEX hash was verified unchanged

decision: Static far stars do not solve the window
next: Owner decision: either authorize one small far-only row-baked visual prototype accepting full-speed ring motion, or end this far-star simplification route. Do not execute automatically.
